items.title: Sal Gutierrez Interview, 1970-01-15
items.q: I played with them. Like Betty Hutton.

ctx.x: It was pretty though. They had blue velvet dresses and they had, that was their theme song, Late in the Evening. That's right. And then there was a nine piece orchestra. It was a beautiful band, but they didn't do too much for that reason. How many girls in the band? Nine. It was like that. You would play with them?
I played with them. Like Betty Hutton.
I played with them in that band. My sister played drum and then Sal played drum. My sister, Lice Perry, Lice Bajon.

items.title: Sal Gutierrez Interview, 1970-01-15
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Oh, you don't like sugar Betty, how? Yeah. You don't like sugar Betty. Yeah.

ctx.x: Oh man. He said trombone player. Oh. Santa Pecola. Without a doubt. Santa. When you're playing at the palace man. I was going to stay in bed. Santa's a good, Santa's a good trombone player in anybody's country. Santa. And all over the country, up that time, Tommy Dorsey, Mithmo, and T. Gordon. Good night, he got so many now, the A-blankin, you know. Mm-hmm. But I mean, back in those days, I liked Mithmo and T. Gordon. What about… Go ahead. Trumpet.
Oh, you don't like sugar Betty, how? Yeah. You don't like sugar Betty. Yeah.
You don't like sugar Betty, how? Yeah.
